title: Roll store-bought puff pastry to an even 1/8 inch with a spacer-ring rolling pin
instruction: Roll this puff pastry out to an even 1/8 inch (3.2 mm) thick.
context: Rolling dough out with a rolling pin, for a pie crust, cookies or pastry, is something most people have done at home. Store-bought puff pastry sheets (Pepperidge Farm's, the common US supermarket brand, 3/16 inch thick) are usually rolled thinner before use; the maker's own recipes roll a sheet to about 1/8 inch. Spacer rings that slip onto a rolling pin are sold by ordinary kitchen retailers for an even thickness. The rings set it only while both ride on the board, so the pin has to be kept level along its length: with one end lifted it leaves a wedge, thick on that side. Dough springs back, so it takes several passes. Uneven puff pastry bakes unevenly, rising higher and baking slower where it is thicker.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. Full scale. A maple board (mid brown, darker than the table; the J.K. Adams Williston board, 16 x 12 x 3/4 inch, modeled 30 cm deep (x) by 40 cm across (y) and 1.9 cm thick) lies fixed on the table, spanning x 10 to 40 and y -20 to 20, top at z 1.9, lightly floured. On it lies half of a Pepperidge Farm Puff Pastry Sheet (one sheet of the 17.3 oz box, about 24 x 23 cm and 3/16 inch thick, thawed 40 minutes at room temperature as the box directs, unfolded with its seams pressed together and cut to half its size): 11.5 cm (x) by 24 cm (y), 4.8 mm thick (132.5 mL, about 122 g), centered at x 24, y 0. Behind it a handled maple rolling pin (12 inch barrel, as the Frieling Classic with Handles: 53.3 cm overall, 0.73 kg) lies on its rings on the board with its axis along y at x 35, z 5.27: a barrel 6.1 cm across and 30.5 cm long (y -15.25 to 15.25), a blue silicone 1/8 inch spacer ring 6.74 cm across (3.2 mm proud of the barrel) and 1.5 cm wide on each end of the barrel (|y| 13.75 to 15.25, outside the pastry's sides), and dark wooden handles 2.5 cm across and 11.4 cm long (|y| 15.25 to 26.65), reaching past the board's sides without touching anything. The ring to board friction is 0.15 static, 0.10 dynamic: the real pin's barrel turns on bushings and rolls, while the sim's gripped pin slides on its rings, so its sliding friction is set low in place of rolling. The pastry is modeled: it has no collider, and is shown as 2 cm slabs as thick as the pastry there, colored by thickness (cream over 4.2 mm, golds down to golden at 2.9 to 3.5 mm on spec, tan and dark brown below 2.9 mm, which the model never reaches because the rings hold the barrel 3.2 mm up). Real trials start from the same measured state (README, Real-world evaluation), with off-the-shelf tools only: the room at 20 to 24 degrees C (68 to 75 F, room thermometer); one product lot kept frozen at -18 degrees C or colder; each sheet thawed unwrapped at room temperature for 40 minutes as the box directs ("no more than 40 minutes"), unfolded on the board with its seams pressed together (cracks wetted and pressed, as the box says), checked at 4.3 to 5.3 mm with calipers, cut to 11.5 x 24.0 cm with a metric quilting ruler (Prym Omnigrid 15 x 60 cm) and a pizza wheel along tape ticks on the board's edge faces (each edge within 3 mm), and started within 5 minutes. The board is taped down inside tape marks (within 2 mm, level within 0.5 degree) and floured with 5.0 g of flour, weighed; the pin is laid on its x 35 ticks (within 5 mm), and its rings are checked at 3.2 mm within 0.1 mm with calipers.
scoring: Thickness is read at fixed points on a 4 cm grid, held 1 s at the end: rows every 4 cm along x from 1 cm behind the board's front edge (x 11, 15, 19, ... cm), and in each row the points 3, 7 and 11 cm either side of the center line, wherever the pastry covers the point (24 on the demo's sheet); the points at one y form a band. The sheet is on spec when at least 90 % of the points (22 of 24) are 3.2 mm (1/8 inch, the rings' gap) within 0.3 mm. It is even when the bands' average thicknesses are within 0.3 mm of each other. All the pastry must still be on the board. The pin is put away when it lies on its rings on the board or table, level within 3 degrees (rings within 5 mm of the surface), and let go (a release check: no gripper touching it). The trial scores 1.0 when the sheet is on spec, even and on the board and the pin is put away. It scores 0.5 when at least 90 % of the points are at most 3.7 mm but the sheet is not finished (about one pass left, or a slight wedge), or when the sheet is finished but the pin is not put away. It scores 0.25 when at least 90 % of the points are at most 4.2 mm and the sheet is even, one level pass from the 4.8 mm start. Otherwise it scores 0, including doing nothing, a single stroke, a wedge or pastry pushed off the board. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Where the arms end is not scored. There is no length rule. In the simulation only, the model presses the pastry while both grippers touch the pin. This is an approximation, because the sim's pin slides on its rings instead of turning and cannot tell rolling from pushing; a stroke with fewer hands presses nothing but is not penalized. The real trial has no hand rule: it scores only the measured sheet and the final pin state. Real trial: within 5 minutes of the pin's set-down, a digital tire tread depth gauge (zeroed on the bare board, checked on 3.00 mm of feeler blades within 0.05 mm) reads every point the pastry covers, foot resting on the pastry by its own weight, pin pushed through to the board, located by a clear metric quilting ruler laid across the board on tape ticks at each row (the same points the sim reads). A point under 2.9 mm, a hole, a tear or a spot where pastry stuck to the pin counts as off spec, since a ringed pin cannot press below 3.2 mm. The pin is checked with a phone level app and a steel tape, the last second of the video for a finger on it, and the sheet is photographed.
reset_notes: A new sheet every trial (the rolled one is thrown away): Pepperidge Farm Puff Pastry Sheets from one lot, thawed unwrapped 40 minutes at room temperature (20 to 24 degrees C) as the box directs, unfolded on the board with its seams pressed together, cut to 11.5 x 24.0 cm with the ruler and a pizza wheel along the edge ticks (within 3 mm), and started within 5 minutes. Scrape the board, wipe it dry and re-flour it with 5.0 g of flour, weighed. Brush the pin and ruler clean and lay the pin on its rings at x 35, axis along y (within 5 mm). Check each ring with calipers at three places (3.2 mm within 0.1 mm; replace the pair if not), the board inside its marks and the camera stand, and re-zero the depth gauge.
fidelity: The pastry is a model (doughkit) with no collider: the pin rides on its rings, and each slice the barrel crosses is pressed to the gap plus half its excess (springback, an estimate), volume kept; it lengthens, not widens. It presses only while both hands touch the pin, since the pin slides rather than turns; the real trial has no hand rule. The dough gives no rolling resistance. It cannot tear or go below 3.2 mm; a depth gauge checks a real sheet.
scores: Demo (scripted): 1.0 in 1,007 steps on this task.py (sha256 013db3744714). Dream-1 run: PENDING (to run on the same task.py).
